extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities and interested public (refund claimants, TSCA test data submitters, FCC applicants, maritime parties, bank applicants, and commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria used across multiple Federal Register notices (DOE refund proceedings, EPA TSCA receipts, FCC hearing designations, FMC agreements, Shipping Act complaints, Federal Reserve applications) describing how claims/applications/tests/comments are to be evaluated, documented, or submitted and the associated deadlines and evidentiary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions of injury for refund claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are end-users, resellers, consignees, or ERA-identified potential claimants may be approved for refunds using applicable presumptions of injury (small claims presumption, reseller/consignee presumption, spot purchaser presumption, end-user presumption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Small-claims and consignee presumptions used for H.A. Mapes, Inc.; applicants who purchased directly and were resellers with allocable share < $5,000 or end-users were granted full allocable share plus proportionate interest (Murphy, Shell decisions). ERA-identified potential claimants who agree to rely on ERA audit files are presumed injured (Pedersen/Irondale Grocery). OHA considered and rejected legal attacks on the spot purchaser presumption (arguments listed: arbitrary/capricious, unsupported by substantial evidence, inconsistent with equitable nature, impermissibly vague, equal protection) but upheld the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate injury for claims over $5,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants whose refund claims exceed $5,000 are required to support their refund claim with a demonstration that they were injured by the pricing practices during the consent order period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Leo's Petroleum was required to and did present injury documentation; DOE evaluated injury documentation before granting refund. When applicants are under common ownership/control and combined allocable share exceeds $5,000, DOE may consolidate applications when applying presumptions of injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation rule for commonly owned applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants are under common ownership and control and their combined allocable share exceeds $5,000, DOE may consolidate the applications for purposes of applying presumptions of injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: State Line Service and Fredericks Fuel Sr Heating Service consolidated because common ownership and combined allocable share exceeded $5,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable proof of claimed volumes (records or reasonable estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may demonstrate the volume underlying their refund claims either by consulting actual records or by using reasonable estimates of their purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: University of Iowa et al. demonstrated volumes by actual records or reasonable estimates. Newark Boxboard used engineering estimation formula for boiler/residual oil: boiler firing rate × hours in a year × years in consent order period × capacity factor = fuel consumed by the boilers. Decisions accept sound engineering principles and specified formulas as basis for volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for claims found to be spurious or subject to defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant's asserted claim is shown to be spurious or subject to defenses (e.g., prior defaults, agency or court orders affecting supply/acceptance), the application may be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Research Fuels, Inc. (RFI) denied because Marathon had defenses including RFI's default on a note, agency orders requiring Marathon to supply downstream purchaser, and court orders precluding acceptance or redirecting supply; DOE concluded the claim was not demonstrated to be non-spurious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting full allocable share plus proportionate interest for small resellers/end-users
rubrics_metrics.description: Resellers with allocable shares less than $5,000 and end-users who purchased directly may be awarded a refund equal to their full allocable share plus a proportionate share of the interest accrued in the escrow account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Murphy Oil decisions, Shell Oil Co. decisions awarding full allocable shares and proportionate interest; sums of principal and interest reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental orders and rescission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE may issue supplemental orders granting additional refunds or rescinding previously granted refunds and order return of funds if refunds were issued improperly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Supplemental Order granting additional refund to Cappy’s Azalea Park Shell for previously unprocessed station gallonage; Supplemental Order rescinding $752 refund to Safeway Shell Tire/Auto and directing return of funds because refund check had been issued in error.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSCA section 4(d) publication requirement for received test data
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(d) of TSCA requires EPA to publish a notice in the Federal Register reporting receipt of test data submitted pursuant to test rules under section 4(a) within 15 days after receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 40 CFR 790.60, consent orders must contain a statement that results will be announced to the public in accordance with section 4(d). EPA established a public record/docket and makes copies of studies available for inspection at specified locations and hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test rule-specific study requirements (cumene, hydroquinone, malononitrile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test rules and consent orders specify particular toxicology/environmental studies that must be submitted for listed chemicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumene (40 CFR 799.1285): 14-week vapor inhalation study in rats with neurotoxicity evaluation; developmental toxicity studies of inhaled vapor in rats and rabbits; disposition and pharmacokinetics following oral, intravenous, or nose-only inhalation; biodegradation study providing mass balance and mineralization/disappearance rates. Hydroquinone (40 CFR 799.2200): 2-generation reproduction study in rats. Malononitrile (40 CFR 799.5000): 90-day oral (gavage) subchronic toxicity study in rats with a four week treatment-free period. These tests are required by the respective test rule/consent order; EPA will initiate review and evaluation but may be initially unable to determine completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and public availability of EPA docket records
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA establishes a public record/docket for TSCA section 4(d) notices (identified by docket number) that includes copies of all studies reported and is available for inspection at a specified office during specified hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: TSCA docket OPTS-44545 available in TSCA Public Docket Office, room NE-G004, 401 M St., SW., Washington, DC, 8 a.m.–4 p.m., Monday–Friday, except legal holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: FMC agreement inspection and comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties may inspect copies of filed agreements at the FMC office and must submit comments to the Secretary within 10 days after the Federal Register notice; comment requirements are in 46 CFR §572.603 and should be consulted beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synopsis of agreement modifications should be provided; the notice identifies Agreement No., Title, Parties, and a brief synopsis of proposed changes (e.g., pool inclusion/exclusions, refrigerated cargo exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipping Act complaint hearing procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints filed under the Shipping Act are assigned to an Administrative Law Judge; hearings, if any, shall commence within the time limitations of 46 CFR 502.61; oral testimony and cross-examination granted only upon proper showing of genuine issues of material fact not resolvable by written evidence; initial and final decision deadlines apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Deppe Line v. Total Tank Distribution assigned to ALJ; hearing commencement and inclusion of oral testimony/cross-examination subject to 46 CFR 502.61; specified deadlines: initial decision by December 28, 1990, final Commission decision by April 29, 1991 (as applied in this notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC comparative hearing issue standardization and designation for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutually exclusive broadcast applications are designated for hearing under section 309(e) with standardized issue headings (Environmental Impact, Air Hazard, Comparative, Ultimate, Financial Qualifications, etc.) as published (text standardized at 51 FR 19347, May 29, 1986); non-standardized issues and the applicants to which they apply are set out in appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice lists applicants and standardized issue headings (letters indicating applicability). Appendices may specify discrete fact-finding issues such as undisclosed party-in-interest, sham organizational structure, and whether an applicant possesses basic qualifications to be a licensee. Complete Hearing Designation Order (HDO) available in FCC Dockets Branch and for purchase from duplicating contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for requesting hearings and contested factual showings (Federal Reserve and other adjudications)
rubrics_metrics.description: When commenters request a hearing on administrative applications (e.g., bank applications), the request must state why a written presentation would not suffice, identify specific questions of fact in dispute, and summarize the evidence to be presented at a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Board of Governors requests for comments on bank change-in-control or bank holding company formation applications must include reasons why written submissions are insufficient and summarize evidence. For administrative hearings (e.g., Shipping Act/ALJ), oral testimony/cross-examination allowed only on proper showing of genuine issues of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 4(c)(8) 'closely related to banking' test criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To approve a bank holding company engaging in a nonbanking activity under section 4(c)(8), the Board considers whether the activity is 'so closely related to banking or managing or controlling banks as to be a proper incident thereto' based on factors such as whether banks generally provide the proposed activity, whether banks provide services operationally or functionally similar to the proposed activity, or whether banks provide services integrally related to the proposed activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may also consider other bases showing a reasonable or close relationship to banking (National Courier Ass'n v. Board of Governors). In applying the test the Board weighs benefits to the public (greater convenience, increased competition, gains in efficiency) against possible adverse effects (undue concentration, decreased or unfair competition, conflicts of interest, unsound banking practices). Applicants should demonstrate benefits and address potential adverse effects and may rely on prior Board precedents (e.g., Morgan, Bankers Trust).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment deadlines and inspection availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices set explicit deadlines by which comments must be received and identify where notices/applications are available for inspection (Federal Reserve Banks, OHA Public Reference Room, FCC Dockets Branch, FMC office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Comments on Change in Bank Control notices must be received by January 18, 1990; bank holding company applications' comments by January 26, 1990; PNC nonbank acquisition comments by January 24, 1990. Copies of full decisions and orders available in specified public reference rooms with stated hours (e.g., OHA Public Reference Room, IE-234, Forrestal Building, 1 p.m.–5 p.m.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural content required in comments requesting hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: A comment requesting a hearing must (a) explain why a written presentation would not suffice, (b) identify specific factual issues in dispute, (c) summarize the evidence that would be presented at a hearing, and (d) indicate how the commenting party would be aggrieved by approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is stated with respect to bank holding company formation/acquisition and section 4(c)(8) applications; similar specificity is required to justify oral hearings in administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior Board/agency precedents and legal rationale in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may rely on prior Board or agency decisions and legal reasoning (e.g., Morgan, Bankers Trust) to justify that proposed activities meet statutory tests or do not raise statutory conflicts (e.g., Section 20 Glass-Steagall concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PNC cited prior Board approvals and rulings to support its contention that proposed private placement and riskless principal activities are closely related to banking and do not raise Section 20 issues; applicants should describe how proposed activities are consistent with precedent and regulatory limitations.
